newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens Medical acquires Apollonio clinic.
newsitem.headline: Athens Medical acquires Apollonio clinic.

text.p: Athens Medical Centre has acquired a majority 85 percent stake in the 130-bed Athens Apollonio Clinic for around 2.8 billion drachmas, Athens Medical's financial officer Yannis Andricopoulos told Reuters.
"The price of the acquisition was around 2.8 billion drachmas, a price earnings ratio (P/E) of 6.5 on a pre-tax basis. The funds have been paid," Andricopoulos said.
Apollonio Clinic had pretax earnings of 500 million drachmas in 1996 on turnover of 2.7 billion. It has a net worth of 875 million, he said.
Projections for this year see pretax profit rising to 800 million drachmas after Athens Medical Centre takes over management.
The 130-bed Apollonio Clinic which offers the full range of medical services had a low occupancy rate of 50 percent. This, however, will rise as it will now service Athens Medical Centre patients.

"Athens Medical Centre has been experiencing high demand for its medical services and since May there has been a waiting list. The acquisition will thus help meet the high demand for the group's medical services," Andricopoulos said.
Of the 85 percent stake, 50 percent was bought by Athens Medical, 20 percent by subsidiary Athens Medical-Paleo Faliro and the remainder by main shareholder and board chairman George Apostolopoulos.
Apollonio Cinic will change its name and hence be a part of the Athens Medical Group.

"There are immediate plans for building new facilities on the adjacent real estate owned by Apollonio. Down the road there are plans for its listing on the Athens stock exchange as it meets profitability requirements," Andricopoulos said.
In the first five months of 1997, Athens Medical Centre's pretax earnings were up 29.4 percent year-on-year at 2.045 billion drachmas on turnover growth of 14.8 percent to 6.2 billion.

During last week's shareholders meeting, board chairman Apostolopoulos told shareholders the company's pretax earnings were expected to grow at an average 22.5 percent between 1996 and 2001. They will reach 9.0 billion in 2001 from 4.2 billion last year, he said.
